entry.name: process-exec-scrub-cloexec
entry.title: tests(process): pin exec_scrub cloexec-only teardown and pipe release
entry.body:
### What
Pins `exec_scrub`: only cloexec ends are closed, their pipes released, surviving fds stay usable, and the call is idempotent.

### Why it matters
exec must drop cloexec descriptors without touching kept ones. No existing test exercises exec_scrub, so inverting the cloexec predicate or miscounting survives.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `entry.cloexec` -> `!entry.cloexec` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| return `0` instead of `count` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib exec_scrub_drops`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

entry.name: instance-validate-bounds

entry.body:
### What
Pins `validate` resource bounds: vcpus 1..=64, memory 16..=1048576; out-of-range rejected, boundary accepted.

### Why it matters
Bounds are fail-closed config gates; widening them admits invalid configs. Existing tests don't pin the exact edges.

entry.name: core-open-readonly
entry.title: tests(core): pin open/openat read-only admission
entry.body:
### What
Pins open(2)/openat(257) admission to read-only: any write access mode or mutating flag is denied.

### Why it matters
The balanced surface is read-only for opens; widening it would admit writes. Existing tests pin writev/wait4 but not open flags.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| drop O_ACCMODE from open mask | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| openat mask -> 0 | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-core --lib open_admission_is_readonly`.

reason: both mutants already killed by existing suite (balanced_contract_allows_read_only_directory_opens) — no genuine gap

entry.name: vfs-overlay-scrub-reuse
entry.title: tests(vfs): scrub unlinked overlay slot before reuse
entry.body:
### What
Pins that an unlinked overlay slot is scrubbed (data zeroed, len reset) before reuse so a fresh overlay never leaks prior bytes.

### Why it matters
Overlay reuse must not expose stale content. Existing tests cover whiteouts but not scrub-on-reuse, so dropping the scrub survives.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| drop `data.fill(0)` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| drop `len = 0` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-vfs --lib unlinked_overlay_slot`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

reason: equivalent mutants on public API: create_overlay() re-zeroes data+len on every reuse, masking release_unlinked scrub; keep-len anchor ambiguous (2 sites)

entry.name: process-retain-refcount
entry.title: tests(process): pin duplicate retain counts and source-close survival

mutants.name: noop-retain
decrement-retain

entry.body:
### What
Pins `retain` via duplicate: both duplicated ends raise the count to 4, closing originals keeps the pipe alive, only the last copy frees it.

### Why it matters
Over-retaining leaks pipe objects; skipping the increment retains nothing and under-counts duplicates. Existing duplicate tests pin single-end retention, not both-ends survival.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| no-op retain (early return) | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| decrement instead of increment | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib duplicate_retains`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

reason: covered: existing pipe_release_frees_only_after_last_end (@2105-2121) pins exact retain counts after duplicate/close; every public-API retain mutant (noop/decrement/+N) is killed by it; live-check unreachable via duplicate lookup guard

entry.name: instance-derive-grants
entry.title: tests(instance): derive write grant from create-only filesystem policy
entry.body:
### What
Pins `derive_contract_grants`: a create-only filesystem policy derives the `filesystem.**` write grant while read stays ungranted.

### Why it matters
Create implies mutation; dropping the create arm or requiring both lists silently unmediates creation paths. Existing recipes always set read+write+create together, so the create-only edge is unpinned.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| drop `|| !filesystem_create...is_empty()` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `||` -> `&&` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-instance --lib create_only_filesystem_grants`.

entry.name: process-pipe-ends-guards

### What
Pins `pipe_ends`: pipe 0 and out-of-range ids report 0, live pipes report their end count, freed slots report 0, reused slots report fresh counts.

### Why it matters
Diagnostics drive leak checks; dropping the zero guard indexes pipe 0 - 1 (underflow) and returning 0 for live pipes misreports leaks. No existing test exercises these edges.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)

entry.name: process-unshare-copy
entry.title: tests(process): pin unshare private-copy, solo no-op, and unknown-task edges
entry.body:
### What
Pins `unshare`: a shared descriptor table is copied privately (pipe ends retained), a solo task is a no-op, and unknown tasks return Ok without allocation.

### Why it matters
Exec unshares files before CLOEXEC scrub; counting zero members or off-by-one on the member threshold either leaks shared fds across exec or double-retains pipes. No existing test exercises unshare.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `**member != 0` -> `== 0` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `> 1` -> `>= 1` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-process --lib unshare_copies_shared`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

entry.name: kernel-views-cgroup-remove-busy
entry.title: tests(kernel-views): pin cgroup remove busy guard for active children
entry.body:
### What
Pins `remove` busy semantics: an active child group blocks parent removal, leaf groups remove cleanly, freed inactive slots never block, root and non-root callers are denied.

### Why it matters
The busy guard chains `active && path != self && parent == path`; flipping any operator lets parents of live children be removed (orphaning confinement) or blocks legitimate cleanup. Existing tests pin only the member-count branch.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| `group.active &&` -> `group.active ||` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| `parent_path(...) == path` -> `!= path` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-kernel-views --lib remove_busy_only`.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed by me.

entry.name: oci-select-manifest-platform
entry.title: tests(oci): pin select_manifest linux/amd64/no-variant platform gate
entry.body:
### What
Pins `select_manifest`: only linux/amd64 with empty variant is selected; wrong OS, wrong arch, or non-empty variant are rejected.

### Why it matters
Platform selection gates which manifest runs; flipping `&&` to `||` admits foreign-OS or variant manifests into the amd64 slot — a confinement-relevant mis-selection. No existing test exercises select_manifest.

### Mutation evidence (fail-then-pass)
| Mutant | Existing suite | New test |
|---|---|---|
| first `&&` -> `||` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |
| second `&&` -> `||` | PASS (survives) | FAIL (killed) |

Baseline: PASS. Reproduce: `cargo test -p ginux-oci --lib select_manifest_requires`.
